items.title: 黃仁勳打破沉默！認了犯錯、願回任輝達 決定權交董事會
items.title_en: Jensen Huang Breaks Silence, Acknowledges Mistakes and Offers to Return as Nvidia CEO if Board Approves
paras: 綜合外媒周二(17日)報導，輝達(NVDA-US)前執行長黃仁勳離任後首次發布公開聲明，表態若董事會認為他的回歸符合股東、員工、公司及美國的最佳利益，他願意回任執行長。他也承認個人生活犯下嚴重錯誤，承諾配合董事會的獨立調查。
黃仁勳表示，離任後收到許多員工、投資人、合作夥伴及客戶呼籲他回任的聲音。
他說：「如果董事會認為，我的回歸符合股東、員工、公司及美國的最佳利益，我將很榮幸回應這些呼聲，重新擔任執行長。」
對於引發離任的風波，黃仁勳坦言，自己未能達到輝達對所有人的要求，並在個人生活中犯下嚴重錯誤。
他說：「我為董事會帶來了問題，對此深感懊悔。我完全承擔自己的錯誤，並承諾配合董事會的獨立調查。」
黃仁勳上周因婚外情風波辭職，結束33年的執行長任期。輝達已委託 Wachtell Lipton 律師事務所，調查他的行為是否危及國家安全或公司機密，包括他與疑涉中國情報活動的黃樂(Alice Huang)之間的關係。
呼籲黃仁勳回任的網路連署已獲逾18萬人支持，馬斯克等科技業人士也加入聲援。美國總統川普周一表示，不反對黃仁勳重新擔任輝達執行長，並認為他已「學到很大的教訓」。
《華爾街日報》另披露，輝達開發者技術主管 Nader Khalil 周一致函董事長瓊斯(Harvey Jones)，呼籲讓黃仁勳回歸。他在信中表示，相信公司終有一天能找到接班人，但不能倉促進行交接，未來幾年的關鍵時期仍需要黃仁勳領導。
不過，《CNBC》與《華爾街日報》均報導，董事會並未考慮讓黃仁勳回任。輝達董事會上周五表示，正挑選協助尋找新執行長的人才招募公司，並於周二宣布成立新委員會，監督國家安全政策與出口管制遵循情況。

黃仁勳聲明全文


過去一周，朋友、業界同仁，以及素未謀面的人們給予的關愛與支持，讓我深受感動。感謝每一位善待我和家人的人，這對我意義重大。
我在53年前來到美國，成為美國公民，是我人生中最珍貴的禮物之一，也是最引以為傲的時刻之一。輝達是我畢生的心血。能與同事們一起，將它打造為今天這樣的公司，是我的榮幸。只有在美國，才有可能誕生像輝達這樣的公司。我愛我們的國家，也愛輝達。
我未能達到輝達對每一個人的要求，也在個人生活中犯下了嚴重錯誤。我為董事會帶來了問題，對此深感懊悔。我完全承擔自己的錯誤，並承諾配合董事會的獨立調查。
自從離任以來，我看到輝達員工、投資人、合作夥伴與客戶，紛紛呼籲我回任執行長。在公司面對複雜的技術、市場、競爭與地緣政治局勢之際，許多人仍持續直接與我聯繫。輝達是一家一個世代才可能出現一次的公司。如果董事會認為，我的回歸符合股東、員工、公司及美國的最佳利益，我將很榮幸回應這些呼聲，重新擔任執行長。
再次感謝所有向我表達祝福的人。你們的支持，讓我深感謙卑。
致我的家人：我愛你們，我會用餘生努力，讓自己值得你們的愛。
paras_en: Comprehensive foreign media reports on Tuesday (the 17th) said that Jensen Huang, former CEO of Nvidia (NVDA-US), issued his first public statement since stepping down, indicating that he would be willing to resume the CEO role if the board believes his return serves the best interests of shareholders, employees, the company and the United States, and he also admitted serious personal mistakes and pledged to cooperate with an independent board investigation.
Huang said that after his departure he received many calls from employees, investors, partners and customers urging him to return.

He said: “If the board believes my return is in the best interests of shareholders, employees, the company and the United States, I would be honored to answer those calls and resume the CEO position.”
Regarding the controversy that led to his resignation, Huang candidly admitted that he failed to meet Nvidia’s expectations of everyone and made serious personal errors.
He said: “I have caused problems for the board and deeply regret it. I fully own my mistakes and commit to cooperating with the board’s independent investigation.”

Huang resigned last week amid an extramarital affair scandal, ending a 33‑year tenure as CEO. Nvidia has hired the law firm Wachtell Lipton to investigate whether his conduct jeopardized national security or company secrets, including his relationship with Alice Huang, who is suspected of ties to Chinese intelligence activities.

A petition calling for Huang’s return has gathered over 180,000 signatures, with tech figures such as Elon Musk joining the support. Former President Donald Trump said on Monday he does not oppose Huang resuming the Nvidia CEO role and believes Huang has “learned a big lesson.”

The Wall Street Journal reported that Nvidia’s senior developer technology officer Nader Khalil sent a letter to chairman Harvey Jones on Monday urging Huang’s comeback, stating he believes the company will eventually find a successor but cannot rush the transition and that the critical coming years still require Huang’s leadership.

However, both CNBC and the Wall Street Journal reported that the board is not considering Huang’s return. Nvidia’s board said last Friday it is selecting a talent‑search firm to help find a new CEO and announced on Tuesday the creation of a new committee to oversee national‑security policy and export‑control compliance.

Full text of Huang’s statement

Over the past week, the care and support from friends, industry colleagues and even strangers have moved me deeply. I thank everyone who has treated my family and me kindly; it means a great deal to me.

I came to the United States 53 years ago and became a citizen – one of the most precious gifts of my life and a source of great pride. Nvidia is the work of my whole life. It has been an honor to build it with my colleagues into the company it is today. Only in America could a company like Nvidia be born. I love our country and I love Nvidia.

I failed to meet Nvidia’s expectations of every individual and made serious personal mistakes. I caused problems for the board and deeply regret it. I fully own my mistakes and commit to cooperating with the board’s independent investigation.

Since stepping down, I have heard Nvidia employees, investors, partners and customers repeatedly urging me to return as CEO. As the company faces complex technical, market, competitive and geopolitical challenges, many continue to reach out to me directly. Nvidia is a once‑in‑a‑generation company. If the board believes my return serves the best interests of shareholders, employees, the company and the United States, I would be honored to answer those calls and resume the CEO role.
Thank you again to everyone who has sent me well‑wishes. Your support makes me feel humbled.
To my family: I love you and will spend the rest of my life working to be worthy of your love.

items.title: 從市場助力到「破壞球」：美元走強為何讓華爾街感到不安？
items.title_en: From Market Support to a ‘Disruptive Force’: Why a Stronger Dollar Is Making Wall Street Uneasy
paras: 美元指數在周二（17日）亞洲交易時段小幅回調0.1%，但周一來到103.7，創19個月新高，華爾街策略師開始擔憂若美元漲勢過快，原本支撐美國資產的強勢美元，反而可能成為加劇美股動盪的「破壞性力量」。
《MarketWatch》報導，美元正重新成為全球金融市場的重要變量。美國經濟表現強於其他主要經濟體、AI基礎設施投資持續吸引海外資金，加上Fed可能進一步升息，推動美元近期加速走強。
美銀全球研究部投資策略師Michael Hartnett上周警告，若美元持續飆升，將成為全球金融市場的「破壞球」，對風險資產構成嚴重威脅。專家指出，美國經濟相對強勁、利率預期偏高，加上AI投資熱潮吸引海外資金，正推升美元走勢。
分析認為，美元升值通常伴隨融資成本上升與金融條件緊縮，對全球股市、債市等風險資產形成普遍壓力。
歷史數據顯示，多數資產與美元呈負相關，僅原油及能源股例外。此外，美元走強將加重以美元借貸的海外企業償債負擔，並可能使國際資金回流美國，進一步壓抑非美市場表現。
在AI浪潮方面，高盛策略師發現，美元漲勢與AI相關股票表現密切連動，無論市場涨跌皆然。AI企業股價走強吸引海外資金湧入，形成「AI股漲—美元升」的正向循環。
高盛預估，美元升值態勢可能延續至2027年，但速度將放緩。不過，若資料中心建設因故減速，AI動能減弱，美元升勢也將面臨回落風險。
Fed後續利率決策仍是關鍵變數。市場預期Fed可能繼續升息，支撐美元偏強格局。
Sevens Report Research創辦人Tom Essaye指出，短期美股或許尚能承受，但若美元指數升至105或更高水平，將開始對標普500等主要指數造成實質衝擊，投資人須嚴防美元過熱引發的金融動盪。
paras_en: The dollar index slipped 0.1% during Asian trading on Tuesday (the 17th), but on Monday it rose to 103.7, a 19‑month high, prompting Wall Street strategists to worry that if the dollar’s rise accelerates, the strong dollar that has been supporting U.S. assets could instead become a “disruptive force” that fuels volatility in U.S. equities.

MarketWatch reports that the dollar is re‑emerging as a key variable in global financial markets. A U.S. economy that is performing better than other major economies, continued overseas inflows into AI infrastructure investments, and the prospect of further Fed rate hikes are all driving the dollar’s recent acceleration.

Bank of America Global Research investment strategist Michael Hartnett warned last week that a persistently soaring dollar would become a “disruptive ball” for global financial markets, posing a serious threat to risk assets. Experts note that a relatively strong U.S. economy, higher‑than‑expected rate expectations, and the AI investment boom attracting foreign capital are all pushing the dollar higher.
Analysts say that dollar appreciation usually comes with higher financing costs and tighter financial conditions, creating broad pressure on global equities, bonds and other risk assets.

Historical data show that most assets have a negative correlation with the dollar, with oil and energy stocks as the only exceptions. A stronger dollar also raises the debt‑servicing burden for overseas companies that borrow in dollars and could trigger a repatriation of international capital to the United States, further dampening performance in non‑U.S. markets.

On the AI front, Goldman Sachs strategists have found that the dollar’s rise is closely linked to the performance of AI‑related stocks, regardless of overall market direction. Strong AI stock gains attract foreign capital, creating a positive feedback loop of “AI stock rally → dollar rise.”

Goldman Sachs projects that the dollar’s appreciation could continue through 2027, albeit at a slower pace. However, if data‑center construction slows for any reason and AI momentum weakens, the dollar’s upward trajectory could face a pull‑back risk.
Future Fed rate decisions remain a key variable. Markets expect the Fed may keep raising rates, supporting a relatively strong dollar environment.

Tom Essaye, founder of Sevens Report Research, notes that U.S. equities may still hold up in the short term, but if the dollar index climbs to 105 or higher, it will begin to deliver material blows to major indices such as the S&P 500, and investors need to guard against financial turbulence sparked by an overheated dollar.

items.title: 47層金色高塔成形！川普圖書館頭七月募5760萬美元 金主來源不透明  ABC、Meta和解金藏多少？
items.title_en: Golden 47‑Story Tower Takes Shape! Trump Library Raises $57.6 Million in First Seven Months, Funding Sources Opaque, How Much of ABC, Meta Settlement Money Is Hidden?
paras: 外媒最新報導指出，美國總統川普籌建總統圖書館的基金會，成立前七個月累計募得5760萬美元，超出原先預期，但資金來源缺乏透明度，未披露捐贈者身份，也無法確認巨額訴訟和解款的實際到帳規模，工程建設用地也面臨法律爭議。
根據《華盛頓郵報》與《CNN》周一(16日)報導，去年稅務申報文件顯示，基金會截至去年底籌得5760萬美元，為川普打算在邁阿密市中心興建的47層樓圖書館提供初步資金。該建築入口採金色裝飾，擬展示一架空軍一號飛機且可能兼具飯店功能。文件中未公開捐贈者名單，也未說明《ABC》、Meta、派拉蒙等企業支付的訴訟和解金在籌款總額中佔比。
基金會原向美國國稅局(IRS)預估2025年底籌資約5000萬美元，實際金額高出760萬美元。基金會曾預估2027年底累計籌資近10億美元，但最新文件未提籌款目標能否實現的資訊。
支出方面，基金會成立前七個月僅花費約34.9萬美元，大部分支付給建築設計公司Bermello Ajamil & Partners，用於製作效果圖。
基金會由五人董事會管理，包括川普次子艾利克、女婿麥可·布洛斯及律師詹姆斯·凱利。文件顯示，去年管理人員及受托人均未支薪。
資金來源受關注的關鍵在於和解安排。2024年大選期間及川普第一任期結束後，他對多家媒體與科技企業提告，部分企業以和解收場並同意撥款。ABC於2024年12月同意支付1500萬美元；Meta於2025年1月指定2200萬美元；《CBS》母公司派拉蒙達成總額1600萬美元和解，扣除費用後餘款轉交，三項和解金合計5300萬美元，但文件未列各筆到帳金額，故無法確認5760萬中有多少直接來自這些和解金。
此外，佛州州長德桑提斯去年協助推動，將邁阿密市中心一塊原屬邁阿密戴德學院、估值約6300萬美元的土地轉交基金會。不過多名南佛州居民已提告阻止，並將川普、基金會、佛州政府及學院列為被告。川普等已請求聯邦法官駁回，爭議未決。
初期籌款雖超預期，基金會距2027年底近10億美元目標仍差距甚遠。在捐款名單與和解金流向未公開下，這座「金色圖書館」的資金透明度與潛在利益衝突疑雲，將持續受公眾檢視。
paras_en: Foreign media reports say the foundation set up to build former President Trump’s presidential library raised $57.6 million in its first seven months, exceeding expectations but lacking transparency about donors and the actual amount of large litigation settlement funds that have been received, while the construction site also faces legal disputes.

According to the Washington Post and CNN on Monday (the 16th), tax filings from last year show the foundation had raised $57.6 million by year‑end, providing seed money for the planned 47‑story library in downtown Miami. The building’s entrance will be gilded, it is slated to display a Air Force One aircraft and may also include a hotel component. The filings do not disclose the list of donors nor explain what share of the total comes from settlement payments by companies such as ABC, Meta and Paramount.

The foundation had originally projected to the IRS that it would raise about $50 million by the end of 2025; the actual amount was $7.6 million higher. It had also forecast nearly $1 billion in cumulative fundraising by the end of 2027, but the latest documents contain no information on whether that target is still realistic.
On the expense side, the foundation spent only about $349,000 in its first seven months, most of which went to the architectural firm Bermello Ajamil & Partners for rendering work.

The foundation is overseen by a five‑member board that includes Trump’s son Eric, son‑in‑law Michael Boulos and lawyer James Kelly. The filings show that none of the managers or trustees received a salary last year.

The source of the money is under scrutiny because of settlement arrangements. During the 2024 election cycle and after Trump left office, he sued several media and tech firms, some of which settled and agreed to fund the foundation. ABC agreed in December 2024 to pay $15 million; Meta earmarked $22 million in January 2025; CBS parent Paramount reached a settlement totaling $16 million, with the balance after fees transferred to the foundation. The three settlements total $53 million, but the filings do not list the amounts actually received, so it is unclear how much of the $57.6 million comes directly from those settlements.

In addition, Florida Governor Ron DeSantis helped last year to transfer a parcel of land in downtown Miami, formerly owned by Miami‑Dade College and valued at about $63 million, to the foundation. Several South‑Florida residents have sued to block the transfer, naming Trump, the foundation, the state government and the college as defendants. Trump and co‑defendants have asked a federal judge to dismiss the case, and the dispute remains unresolved.

Although early fundraising exceeded expectations, the foundation is still far from its near‑$1 billion goal for the end of 2027. With donor lists and settlement flows undisclosed, the financial transparency and potential conflicts of interest surrounding the “golden library” will continue to draw public scrutiny.

paras_en: U.S. equity turbulence continued to drive foreign investors out, putting the Taiwan market under a fresh wave of sell‑off pressure on the 17th. With the National Security Fund stepping in to support, the market narrowly held the psychological 40,000‑point barrier. In the Taipei foreign‑exchange market, the central bank intervened to maintain dynamic stability; the New Taiwan dollar briefly slipped past the 33‑per‑U.S.‑dollar mark but recovered in the last half‑hour, closing at 32.85, a gain of 0.036. Transaction volume at Taipei FX brokers surged to $2.824 billion, indicating a fierce tug‑of‑war between buyers and sellers.

The New Taiwan dollar opened at 32.89, down 0.004, and as the Taiwan stock index swung wildly it fell as low as 33.015. Among major Asian currencies, the Korean won showed the largest volatility but was down only about 0.1%. The U.S. Dollar Index hovered near flat. The Singapore dollar and the Chinese yuan each edged up less than 0.05%, the New Taiwan dollar rose 0.11%, the Japanese yen jumped roughly 0.15%, and the Thai baht rebounded about 0.2%.

Institutional investors note that after Jensen Huang’s departure, rumors surfaced that Nvidia’s new Rubin server rollout would be delayed, leaving doubts over the broader AI sector. This prompted domestic leveraged positions to unwind. Although bullish forces managed to keep the market above the 40,000‑point line today, the overall trend remained weak, fostering a pessimistic atmosphere. Nvidia’s first earnings call without Huang is set to take place, and market reaction will need close monitoring.

items.title: 強美元恐成全球股市破壞球 華爾街緊盯105關鍵警戒線
items.title_en: Strong Dollar May Become a Global Market Disruptor, Wall Street Watches the Critical 105 Threshold
paras: 美元漲勢加速，華爾街開始警戒強美元對股市的衝擊。美國經濟韌性、人工智慧（AI）資本支出熱潮與升息預期，持續吸引海外資金流入，但美元走強也可能推升借貸與償債壓力。美銀警告，若美元延續目前漲勢，恐成為衝擊全球市場的「破壞球」。
根據FactSet數據，ICE美元指數周一(16日)一度觸及103.69，創2025年4月2日以來最高。
美銀全球研究投資策略師Michael Hartnett在近期客戶報告中指出：「如果美元按照這種節奏繼續飆升，它終將演變成一顆破壞球。」
Manulife John Hancock Investments聯席首席投資策略師Emily Roland表示，美元近期走強，主要受到市場預期聯準會可能持續升息，以及美國經濟相較其他經濟體更具韌性所帶動。
她更擔心的是，這波升勢反映市場預期借貸成本將進一步提高，而這通常會壓抑全球風險資產。
Roland提醒，美元走強期間，美股表現通常優於非美股市，但市場接下來仍可能面臨金融環境收緊的考驗。美國大型優質股通常更有能力抵禦風險，資金最終可能轉向資產負債表健全、現金流充沛的企業。
她與同僚Matt Miskin分析美元與各類資產的長期相關性後發現，多數資產與美元呈負相關，意味美元升值時，這些資產往往承壓。兩人在報告中指出，原油及能源類股是少數與美元維持弱正相關的資產類別。
強美元也將加重部分海外企業的負擔。Roland表示，對於背負美元債務、本國貨幣卻走貶的企業而言，美元匯率上升將顯著推高償債成本。
這波美元強勢，與去年的走勢形成鮮明對比。2025年ICE美元指數大幅走弱，寫下有紀錄以來最差年度表現之一；今年則受惠於較穩健的美國經濟基本面，吸引追求超額報酬的海外資金流入，進一步鞏固美元強勢。
高盛策略師指出，今年美元走強，也與預期受惠於AI的企業股價優於大盤有關。團隊表示，無論市場行情好壞，美元表現似乎都與AI相關股票的走勢存在關聯。
除了AI熱潮，美國利率上升也提高美元吸引力。高盛預期，美元強勢將延續至2027年，升值趨勢仍將持續，但步伐可能放緩。
不過，AI投資動能也可能左右美元後續走勢。Roland認為，AI已是當前經濟成長不可或缺的核心引擎，若算力瓶頸或建設週期等因素導致資料中心建設放緩，美元加速上漲的動能也可能隨之降溫。
Sevens Report Research創辦人兼總裁Tom Essaye則認為，市場對聯準會進一步升息的預期，仍將為美元提供支撐。
他提醒，儘管股市目前可能尚屬安全，一旦ICE美元指數突破105，甚至更高的關鍵阻力位，強美元的外溢效應恐對美股主要指數造成實質打擊。
paras_en: The dollar's rally is accelerating, prompting Wall Street to warn of its impact on equity markets. US economic resilience, a surge in AI‑related capital spending and expectations of further rate hikes continue to draw overseas capital, but a stronger dollar could also raise borrowing and debt‑service pressures. Bank of America warns that if the dollar maintains its current rise, it could become a "disruptive ball" that hits global markets.
According to FactSet data, the ICE Dollar Index touched 103.69 on Monday (the 16th), the highest level since April 2, 2025.
Bank of America Global Research investment strategist Michael Hartnett wrote in a recent client note: "If the dollar keeps soaring at this pace, it will eventually turn into a disruptive ball."

Manulife John Hancock Investments co‑Chief Investment Strategist Emily Roland said the dollar’s recent strength is mainly driven by market expectations that the Fed may keep raising rates and by the US economy’s relative resilience compared with other economies.
She added that she is concerned this rally reflects market expectations of higher borrowing costs, which typically suppress global risk assets.

Roland cautioned that while a strong dollar usually sees US equities outperform non‑US markets, the market may still face tightening financial conditions. Large‑cap, high‑quality US stocks are generally better positioned to weather risk, and capital may ultimately flow to companies with strong balance sheets and robust cash flows.

After analyzing the long‑term correlation between the dollar and various assets with colleague Matt Miskin, she found that most assets have a negative correlation with the dollar, meaning they tend to be pressured when the dollar appreciates. In their report they noted that crude oil and energy stocks are among the few asset classes that maintain a weak positive correlation with the dollar.

A strong dollar also adds burden to some overseas firms. Roland said that for companies carrying dollar‑denominated debt while their local currencies depreciate, a higher dollar exchange rate will significantly increase debt‑service costs.

This dollar strength contrasts sharply with last year’s trend. In 2025 the ICE Dollar Index weakened sharply, posting one of the worst annual performances on record; this year, buoyed by a more solid US economic foundation, it has attracted overseas capital seeking excess returns, further cementing the dollar’s strength.

Goldman Sachs strategists pointed out that this year’s dollar rally is also linked to expectations that AI‑benefiting stocks will outperform the broader market. The team said that regardless of market conditions, the dollar’s performance appears tied to the trajectory of AI‑related equities.

Beyond the AI boom, rising US rates have also boosted the dollar’s appeal. Goldman Sachs expects the dollar’s strength to persist through 2027, with the appreciation trend continuing, albeit at a potentially slower pace.

However, AI investment momentum could also influence the dollar’s future path. Roland believes AI is now an indispensable engine of economic growth, and if factors such as compute bottlenecks or construction cycles slow data‑center builds, the momentum behind a faster‑rising dollar could cool off.
Tom Essaye, founder and president of Sevens Report Research, said market expectations of further Fed rate hikes will continue to support the dollar.

He warned that although the stock market may still seem safe for now, once the ICE Dollar Index breaks above 105—or even higher key resistance levels—the spill‑over effects of a strong dollar could deliver a tangible hit to major US equity indices.

items.title: 紐西蘭央行意外暫停升息引發拋售 紐元跌至6年低點
items.title_en: New Zealand Central Bank Unexpectedly Pauses Rate Hikes Triggering Sell‑off, Kiwi Falls to 6‑Year Low
paras: 紐西蘭元兌美元匯率周二(17日)跌破 0.55 美元大關，至 0.5490 附近，創下自 2020 年 3 月新冠疫情爆發以來的近6年新低。紐元在今年前 8 個月曾上漲逾 2%，名列 G10 貨幣中表現最佳者之一，但自 8 月高點以來已重挫超過 8%，轉為表現最差的 G10 貨幣。
本輪拋售潮的主因在於紐西蘭央行(RBNZ)在 10 月底以 4 比 3 的票數，決定將官方現金利率維持在 2.75% 不變，出乎原本預期升息機率高達 95% 的金融市場意料。此外，紐西蘭最新公布的5年通膨預期降至 2023 年第一季以來新低，加上失業率攀升至 11 年高點，凸顯國內經濟復甦仍顯脆弱。
National Australia Bank外匯策略全球主管Ray Attrill對此指出：「紐西蘭央行在 10 月放棄升息讓所有人大感吃驚，已被市場視為落後於政策曲線。」
與此同時，市場預期美國聯準會(Fed)將維持鷹派升息立場，使得美紐兩國利差顯著擴大，紐西蘭與美國 10 年期指標公債殖利率差一度擴大至負 48 個基點，創下 2019 年 12 月以來最大差距。
紐西蘭銀行高級策略師Jason Wong分析：「鑑於紐西蘭與美國之間龐大的負利差，加上紐央行採取抵抗升息的態度，紐元弱勢十分合理；在美元獲得良好支撐下，紐元阻力最小的路徑就是繼續下探。」
澳盛集團(ANZ)策略師David Croy團隊也在報告中表示：「紐元最大的阿基里斯腱無疑是低利率環境，這使得從套利角度持有紐元成本極高。」團隊並警告，相對利差將持續在可預見的未來帶來逆風。
ITC Markets 高級外匯分析師Sean Callow表示，雖然市場已預期 12 月有 90% 機率升息，但隨後的決策會議要等到隔年 2 月 10 日，對交易員而言相當漫長。「在科技股波動與聯準會鷹派擔憂下，紐西蘭作為對貿易敏感的小型經濟體，極易受全球動盪衝擊。」
paras_en: The New Zealand dollar fell below the 0.55 USD mark on Tuesday (the 17th), trading around 0.5490, marking its lowest level in nearly six years since the COVID‑19 outbreak in March 2020. The kiwi had risen more than 2% in the first eight months of the year, ranking among the best‑performing G10 currencies, but has since slumped over 8% from its August peak to become the worst‑performing G10 currency.

The main driver of the sell‑off was the Reserve Bank of New Zealand’s (RBNZ) decision at the end of October, by a 4‑to‑3 vote, to keep the official cash rate unchanged at 2.75%, surprising markets that had priced a 95% probability of a hike. In addition, New Zealand’s latest five‑year inflation expectations fell to their lowest since Q1 2023, and the unemployment rate rose to an 11‑year high, underscoring the fragility of the domestic economic recovery.

Ray Attrill, global head of foreign‑exchange strategy at National Australia Bank, said: “The RBNZ’s decision to forgo a rate hike in October caught everyone off guard and is now seen by the market as lagging behind the policy curve.”

At the same time, markets expect the U.S. Federal Reserve to maintain a hawkish stance, widening the NZD‑USD interest‑rate differential. The spread between New Zealand and U.S. 10‑year benchmark bond yields briefly widened to –48 basis points, the largest gap since December 2019.

Senior strategist Jason Wong of New Zealand‑based bank ANZ explained: “Given the large negative differential between New Zealand and the United States, combined with the RBNZ’s resistance to further hikes, the kiwi’s weakness is entirely reasonable; with the dollar firmly supported, the path of least resistance for the kiwi is to keep sliding lower.”

ANZ strategist David Croy’s team also noted in their report: “The kiwi’s biggest Achilles’ heel is undoubtedly the low‑rate environment, which makes holding the currency extremely costly from an arbitrage perspective.” The team warned that the relative yield differential will continue to pose headwinds in the foreseeable future.

Sean Callow, senior FX analyst at ITC Markets, said that although the market now sees a 90% chance of a rate hike in December, the next decision meeting won’t be until February 10 next year, a long wait for traders. “With tech‑stock volatility and Fed hawkish concerns, New Zealand – a trade‑sensitive small economy – is highly vulnerable to global turbulence.”

美國聯邦準備理事會(FED)官員鷹派發言及通貨膨脹數據強勁，激發市場押注FED將採取激進措施以遏制生活成本壓力，而且美國聯邦基金利率期貨暗示，FED在12月8-9日會議升息25個基點基本成定局，加息50個基點的概率則降至6%，但仍預期明年年底前累計升息90個基點，推升美國公債收益率，提供美元撐；此外，週一日本政府數據顯示第三季國內生產總值(GDP)環比年率意外跌0.1%，為四季以來首次萎縮，但除非疲軟態勢蔓延至工資、服務業及基礎國內需求，否則不大可能使日本央行(BOJ)偏離緊縮路徑，並據BOJ審議委員高田創呼籲BOJ必須盡早上調政策利率至適當水平，防範通貨膨脹上行，而且BOJ公布11月會議紀錄顯示，總裁植田和男向政府一個重要委員會表示近期薪資增長強勁，與通貨膨脹可持續達2%目標步伐相符，激勵日圓上漲，美元兌日圓自159.88高點走低。
隨後數據顯示紐約聯邦儲備銀行11月製造業指數驟降至7.80，並據克利夫蘭聯邦儲備銀行總裁哈瑪克稱傾向小幅升息，而且市場關注週四美國總統川普與中國國家主席習近平及俄羅斯總統普丁在亞太經合組織(APEC)會議會面，影響國際局勢發展，引發美元兌日圓回落至159.33低點。預估今日美元兌日圓阻力於159.50-70，支撐於158.50-70。
◆EUR/USD
市場押注FED將大幅加息抑制通貨膨脹，帶動美國公債收益率攀升及美元全線走強，相較澳洲與紐西蘭兩國債券收益率未能跟上美國公債收益率升勢，抹去此前支撐澳幣與紐元的利差優勢，而且澳洲央行(RBA)料明年轉向降息，昨日衝擊澳幣連續第五個交易日下跌至十個月新低，紐元亦下挫至十九個月低位，拖累歐元兌美元於1.1033高點承壓。
據歐洲央行(ECB)副總裁武伊契奇表示，近期能源價格走勢可能會推高通貨膨脹，但信心減弱和信貸成本上升料將拖累經濟增長，並在一定程度上遏制過高的通貨膨脹，而且歐元區9月工業生產較前月增長0.2%及較去年同期下降1.5%遜於預期，打擊歐元兌美元至1.0990低點。預估今日歐元兌美元阻力於1.1000-20，支撐於1.0920-40。
◆GBP/USD

英國央行(BOE)首席經濟學家皮爾在金融時報專訪稱，為抑制通貨膨脹，英國央行(BOE)在12月會議加息外，明年可能需要進一步升息，但英國房地產網站Rightmove週一表示截至11月7日的四周內，英國房屋要價較前月跌1.8%，大於過去十年同期平均1.1%跌幅，突顯伊朗戰爭導致高抵押貸款利息成本，擠壓潛在購房者能力，打擊英鎊兌美元受限於1.3252高點。隨著BOE本月進行三年多來首次升息，數名貨幣政策委員會(MPC)委員可能在12月會議投票支持再加息，激發英國兩年期公債收益率創2023年10月以來最高達5%以上，但市場等待英國本周公布就業和通貨膨脹數據，以重新評估英鎊走勢，打壓英鎊兌美元至1.3174低點。預估今日英鎊兌美元阻力於1.3185-1.3205，支撐於1.3100-20。

items.title: 〈紐約匯市〉美元升至2025年4月來最高 交易員押注Fed升息
paras: 美元週一(16日)升至2025年4月以來最高，兌主要貨幣持續走強。上週公布的通膨數據高於預期，加上聯準會(Fed)官員釋出鷹派訊號，支撐美元近期漲勢。
紐約尾盤，追蹤美元兌六種主要貨幣的美元指數(DXY)上漲0.1%，報103.50，創2025年4月2日以來最高。
歐元兌美元下跌0.1%，報1.1007美元。
美國總統川普去年4月公布「解放日」關稅政策後，市場擔憂美國資產吸引力下降，美元一度大幅走弱。不過，隨著美國經濟展現穩健成長，股市表現也相當強勁，美元已逐步收復失土，部分恢復美國資產對投資人的吸引力。
上週公布的通膨數據偏熱，加上市場押注聯準會可能進一步升息，近期進一步推升美元。
宏觀研究與策略公司Macro Hive研究員Benjamin Ford表示，「在通膨壓力仍令人不安，且2027年可能出現更鷹派政策意外的情況下，年底前歐元兌美元匯率跌至1.08，並非不可能。」
上週公布的數據顯示，美國10月消費者物價漲幅高於預期，進一步鞏固市場對聯準會下個月升息的預期。
通膨數據公布後，市場一度提高對聯準會12月會議升息2碼的押注。此前，聯準會理事華勒(Christopher Waller)曾提出，若通膨數據達到一定門檻，便可考慮加快升息步調。
根據芝商所FedWatch工具，聯邦基金利率期貨目前反映，市場預期聯準會在12月9日結束的下一次為期兩天的政策會議上，升息1碼的機率達95%。
Macro Hive的Ford在報告中指出，「聯準會短期內恐難以擺脫通膨壓力，原因有二。首先，透過各地區調查推算的全國隱含通膨指標，顯示價格壓力正在加速升溫。」
他接著表示，「其次，通膨升溫之際，企業利潤率也有所改善，代表企業能將較高成本轉嫁給消費者，而薪資調漲的可能性也正在增加。」
聯準會主席華許(Kevin Warsh)週一表示，新興科技將對經濟產生重大影響，但未來可能出現不同情境：一種是經濟成長加速，且成長成果廣泛共享，另一種則是，如果預期中的投資報酬不如預期，可能導致失業率上升，甚至經濟成長放緩。
交易員接下來將關注AI產業指標企業輝達(NVDA-US)週二公布的第三季財報，以及Anthropic本週的市場首秀，藉此判斷投資人的風險偏好。

美元兌日元下跌0.2%，至159.38日元。市場正在評估日本經濟數據對日本銀行(BoJ)貨幣政策可能造成的影響。數據顯示，日本今年7月至9月經濟以年化計算萎縮0.1%。
日元目前仍接近市場認為美日當局今年稍早曾進場干預的價位。
State Street Investment Management東京首席固定收益策略師Masahiko Loo表示，「除非疲弱情況進一步擴散至薪資、服務業及國內基本需求，否則日本央行可能會選擇忽略這段短期低迷。」
美元走強也對英鎊造成壓力，英鎊兌美元下跌0.2%，至1.3191美元。交易員正等待本週稍晚公布的英國就業成長及通膨數據。

items.title: AI賺進大把美元 台幣為何還在貶？外媒揭台企資金留海外
items.title_en: AI Generates Massive Dollars, Why Is the New Taiwan Dollar Still Depreciating? Foreign Media Reveal Taiwanese Companies Keep Funds Overseas
paras: 據外媒周一(16日)報導，人工智慧(AI)熱潮帶動台灣經濟與出口強勁成長，新台幣卻持續逼近近十年低點。關鍵在於，企業賺進的美元未必換回台幣，而是留在海外支應擴產與投資，加上外資大舉賣超台股，抵銷出口榮景原本可能帶來的升值動能。
台灣經濟已連續四季維持雙位數成長，為近40年來最長紀錄，經常帳順差規模居全球第四。光是台積電(2330-TW)與鴻海(2317-TW)，第三季合計營收就約達1,400億美元。然而，新台幣今年以來仍貶值逾4%，呈現經濟強、匯率弱的兩樣情。

企業美元留海外 擴產投資排擠換匯需求

法國巴黎銀行估計，台灣企業自2020年以來，已在離岸帳戶累積約2,400億美元，支應對外投資與全球產能擴張。央行近期雖試圖引導出口美元回流、增加台幣需求，仍未能扭轉匯率弱勢。
法國外貿銀行亞太首席經濟學家Alicia Garcia Herrero表示，央行積極希望出口商將美元收入換成台幣，但企業意願不高。
企業保留美元有實際營運需求。台積電幾乎所有營收都以美元收取，超過一半設備款項須支付至海外；廣達(2382-TW)則持有約320億美元的美元資產，同時有約310億美元外幣負債，降低將資金換成台幣的必要性。
地緣政治與生產基地分散也推動資金外移。政府資料顯示，今年截至9月，核准對外投資金額達創紀錄的660億美元，接近2025年全年的兩倍，其中流向北美的金額年增逾六倍。

出口收入未必換台幣 外資賣股再添壓力

美元資金即使留在國內，也未必轉為台幣。央行資料顯示，9月外幣存款攀升至新台幣10兆元的歷史新高，主要由企業帳戶帶動，反映美元較高收益與營運需求的吸引力。
華僑銀行外匯策略師Christopher Wong指出，台灣第二季經常帳順差約585億美元，但金融帳資產淨增加約538億美元，兩者規模接近，反映居民持有美元存款與海外投資資產的需求。
這意味著，強勁出口雖能創造大量美元收入，卻不一定帶來等量的台幣淨買盤。
外資賣股進一步加重壓力。今年以來，外資淨賣超台股達創紀錄的新台幣3兆元。台股在新興市場指數的權重增加，加上市場對AI估值的疑慮，促使海外基金獲利了結。
央行總裁楊金龍周一向立委表示，10月至11月初進場調節匯市的頻率增加，近期匯率波動主要與外資賣股匯出有關，而非台美利差。

美元保單與股息安排 台幣面臨結構性變化

除了企業與外資動向，金融商品的變化也可能減少台幣買盤。台灣壽險業持有約7,000億美元海外資產，業者積極向本地家庭銷售美元計價保單，帶動美元需求。
加拿大皇家銀行資本市場亞洲宏觀策略師Abbas Keshvani指出，美元保單將匯率風險轉由保戶承擔，而一般家庭較少像金融機構一樣進行匯率避險，因此可能減少原本透過賣出美元進行避險、間接支撐台幣的交易。
企業股息安排也可能強化這項趨勢。台積電計畫自2027年起，直接以美元向外國投資人配發股息。此舉雖有助降低季節性換匯造成的市場波動，也會減少美元兌換台幣的交易需求。
Keshvani認為，以美元配息是美元化的一種形式。股東收到美元後，可能保留部分美元資產，進而增加美元需求，或降低對台幣的需求。
paras_en: According to foreign media on Monday (the 16th), the AI boom is driving strong growth in Taiwan’s economy and exports, yet the New Taiwan dollar continues to edge toward a ten‑year low. The key is that the dollars earned by firms are not necessarily converted back into NT$, but are kept overseas to fund expansion and investment, while large foreign‑fund outflows selling Taiwanese stocks offset the appreciation pressure that export strength could have created.

Taiwan’s economy has posted double‑digit growth for four consecutive quarters—the longest streak in about 40 years—and its current‑account surplus ranks fourth globally. Just TSMC (2330‑TW) and Foxconn (2317‑TW) together reported roughly $140 billion in revenue for Q3. Nevertheless, the NT$ has depreciated more than 4% so far this year, reflecting a paradox of a strong economy and a weak currency.

Taiwanese firms have been holding dollars overseas to finance expansion and investment, crowding out demand for currency conversion. BNP Paribas estimates that since 2020 Taiwanese companies have accumulated about $240 billion in offshore accounts to support foreign investment and global capacity expansion. Although the central bank has recently tried to steer export dollars back home and boost NT$ demand, it has not yet reversed the currency weakness.

Alicia Garcia Herrero, chief economist for Asia‑Pacific at France’s Trade and Development Bank, said the central bank is actively encouraging exporters to convert their dollar earnings into NT$, but corporate willingness remains low.

Companies retain dollars for genuine operational needs. TSMC receives almost all of its revenue in dollars, and more than half of its equipment payments are made overseas; Quanta (2382‑TW) holds about $32 billion in dollar assets while also carrying roughly $31 billion of foreign‑currency liabilities, reducing the incentive to swap those funds into NT$.

Geopolitical factors and the dispersion of production bases also push capital abroad. Government data show that by September this year, approved outbound investment reached a record $66 billion, nearly twice the amount projected for the whole of 2025, with funds flowing to North America growing more than six‑fold year‑on‑year.

Even dollars kept domestically are not always turned into NT$. Central bank data indicate that foreign‑currency deposits surged to a historic NT$10 trillion in September, driven mainly by corporate accounts, reflecting the appeal of higher dollar yields and operational needs.

Christopher Wong, foreign‑exchange strategist at Overseas Chinese Bank, noted that Taiwan’s current‑account surplus in Q2 was about $58.5 billion, while net financial‑account asset inflows were roughly $53.8 billion, a near‑parity that mirrors households’ demand for dollar deposits and overseas investment assets.
This means that robust export earnings can generate large dollar inflows without necessarily creating an equivalent net buying pressure for NT$.

Foreign investors’ net selling of Taiwanese stocks adds further pressure. So far this year, foreign investors have sold a record NT$3 trillion worth of shares. The weight of Taiwanese equities in emerging‑market indices has risen, and concerns over AI‑related valuations have prompted overseas funds to take profits.

Central Bank Governor Yang Jin‑long told legislators on Monday that the frequency of market‑stabilising interventions increased from October to early November, and recent exchange‑rate swings are mainly linked to foreign‑fund outflows from stock sales rather than the US‑Taiwan interest‑rate differential.

Dollar‑denominated insurance policies and dividend practices also pose structural challenges for the NT$. Taiwan’s life‑insurance industry holds about $700 billion in overseas assets and is actively selling dollar‑priced policies to local families, boosting dollar demand.

Abbas Keshvani, macro‑strategy analyst for Asian capital markets at RBC, explained that dollar policies shift exchange‑rate risk to policyholders, who unlike financial institutions rarely hedge currency exposure, potentially reducing the traditional dollar‑selling hedges that indirectly support the NT$.

Corporate dividend policies may reinforce this trend. TSMC plans to start paying dividends to foreign investors directly in dollars from 2027. While this could smooth seasonal currency‑conversion volatility, it will also cut the volume of dollar‑to‑NT$ transactions.

Keshvani sees dollar‑denominated dividends as a form of dollarisation. Shareholders receiving dollars may retain part of those assets, increasing dollar demand and further lowering demand for the NT$.
